item.title: Version 0.2.16
item.description:
Says which library is missing when a Homebrew upgrade breaks openconnect.

  • Upgrading a Homebrew library that openconnect depends on (e.g. nettle 3 → 4) can leave openconnect unable to start at all, because the library file it links against was renamed. Connect then fails with the dependency check reporting only "openconnect failed to run" — and, because the sudo permission check runs through the same binary, it wrongly reported the sudo rule as broken too, sending the diagnosis in the wrong direction entirely
  • The dependency row now names the exact missing library, and its Fix button runs brew upgrade openconnect instead of brew install, which does nothing on an already-installed version. If Homebrew has not yet published a rebuilt version, the app says so and points at the source rebuild rather than reporting a successful fix that changed nothing
  • A --version that hangs is reported as a timeout, and other failures now include openconnect's own first error line

item.title: Version 0.2.15
item.description:
Reconnects by itself after the connection dies unexpectedly.

  • When the openconnect process exits while connected — most commonly the Mac slept long enough for the server-side session cookie to expire, so openconnect's own resume gets a 401 and gives up — the app now re-authenticates from scratch with a fresh one-time code instead of sitting disconnected until you click Connect
  • The automatic retry is skipped while the network is down (the existing network-recovery reconnect handles that case) and runs at most once per minute, so an unstable gateway is never hammered

item.title: Version 0.2.14
item.description:
Fixes a self-inflicted login failure after disconnecting.

  • Two connection attempts could start at once — typically an auto-reconnect racing a menu click — and both would generate the same one-time code. The gateway accepts it once and rejects the second as a replay with a 401 that looks exactly like a wrong OTP. Retrying inside the same 30-second window hit the same wall, and three failures then triggered the 5-minute cooldown. Connect attempts are now mutually exclusive
  • A one-time code that has already been submitted is never reused; the app waits for the next 30-second step instead

item.title: Version 0.2.13
item.description:
Two login failures that are impossible to spot by eye.

  • The password and TOTP fields now force the input source to English while you type in them. With a Chinese input method active, typing ! produces the full-width ！ — one character just like the real one, shown as the same dot behind the mask, and silently rejected by the gateway as a wrong password
  • Saving credentials that still contain non-ASCII characters (e.g. pasted from elsewhere) now shows the offending characters and asks for confirmation, and the connect log flags them by code point
  • Fixed passwordless sudo never taking effect for macOS logins containing a dot (e.g. first.last): sudo silently ignores files in /etc/sudoers.d/ whose names contain a ., so the rule was written correctly and then never loaded. The filename is now sanitized and any stale dotted file removed. Thanks to @tianxia-- for finding and fixing this

item.title: Version 0.2.11
item.description:
Fixes authentication against gateways that only accept the official Cisco client.

  • The app now identifies itself as AnyConnect Windows 4.10.06079. Some gateways serve openconnect's own User-Agent an HTTP Basic challenge instead of the OTP form, so the OTP step always failed with 401 — while the official Cisco client on the same machine connected fine. Existing installs pick this up automatically; configurable under Settings → Advanced → User-Agent, leave empty to send openconnect's default
  • Connect attempts are now rate-limited: after 3 consecutive failures the app waits 5 minutes before retrying, so repeated failures don't get your IP banned by the gateway
  • Failure logs now record the real HTTP status instead of only openconnect's misleading fallback message about Basic authentication. Session cookies are redacted
  • The connect log records the two-step setting, credential field lengths, handshake duration, the generated TOTP code and the local clock offset, so an authentication failure can be diagnosed from the log alone

item.title: Version 0.2.8
item.description:
• Two-step login support: new "Server asks for password and OTP separately" toggle for gateways that request the password and OTP in two prompts (e.g. ocserv). In this mode the Password prefix field holds your full password
  • Fix: reconnecting right after a disconnect could leave a live tunnel with no routes (old session's cleanup deleted the new session's routes) — connect now waits for the previous openconnect to fully exit
  • Watchdog now logs the openconnect stderr tail when the tunnel dies unexpectedly, plus clearer OTP-rejection errors

item.title: Version 0.2.7
item.description: • First-time setup now auto-triggers a connection when you click "Done" on the final onboarding step — no more digging into the menu to start the first connect

item.title: Version 0.2.6
item.description:
• Added a new Settings toggle "Auto-connect on launch" — when enabled, the app automatically connects to VPN about 5 seconds after launch
  • The auto-connect only fires when setup is complete (all required fields filled), so it never triggers spurious failures on a half-configured install
  • Once the auto-connect handshake succeeds, the existing network-drop auto-reconnect path takes over, so switching WiFi or sleeping/waking transparently recovers the tunnel

item.title: Version 0.2.5
item.description:
Hotfix — strongly recommended for v0.2.3 / v0.2.4 users.

  • Fixed a case where a failed openconnect handshake could leave a zombie child behind, with vpnc-script's DNS and route mutations applied but never reverted — symptom: "WiFi connected but nothing has network access" until the user quit the app. connect() now always SIGTERMs any residual child on failure so vpnc-script's disconnect phase runs and restores DNS/routes.
  • Pre-connect route flush now only deletes when the kernel returns a concrete IPv4 destination. Previously, when no dedicated host route existed, `route get` fell through to the default route (destination="default") and the subsequent delete wiped the system default route.

item.title: Version 0.2.4
item.description:
• Log files are now split by day — ~/Library/Logs/VPNMenuBar/vpnmenubar-YYYY-MM-DD.log — so individual files stay small and are easy to pick through by date when reporting issues
  • Logs older than 14 days are auto-purged at launch, no disk buildup
  • "Show Logs…" and Settings → Reveal in Finder now always land on the current day's file

item.title: Version 0.2.3
item.description:
• Pre-connect route flush is now unconditional — fixes the case where a cached host route to the VPN gateway looks "correct" (matches the default gateway) but traffic still fails to route after a WiFi/network change
  • Previously the cleanup only deleted routes that looked obviously stale; now it always flushes before spawning openconnect, because at that moment no active tunnel exists and the kernel rebuilds the route on the next packet
  • Each connect attempt now logs the pre-connect flush result (route IP, previous gateway, delete success/failure) so "stuck" connections are diagnosable from the log

item.title: Version 0.2.2
item.description:
• Auto-strip whitespace and invisible characters (zero-width, NBSP, full-width space, newlines) from credential fields on save AND on load — fixes silent failures from pasting values out of chat apps / PDFs
  • Added persistent file log at ~/Library/Logs/VPNMenuBar/vpnmenubar.log covering launch banner, full connect flow, dependency checks, network/interface changes, unexpected disconnects, and dependency-install results
  • Added "Show Logs…" menu item and "Reveal in Finder" button under Settings for quick access to the log
  • Sensitive fields (password prefix, TOTP secret, generated code) are never written to the log

item.title: Version 0.2.1
item.description:
• Redesigned status bar icon: white badge with cutout shield and colored status dot
  • Gateway and server cert pin are now required fields in onboarding
  • Settings save now closes the window and auto-reconnects
  • Save button disabled when no changes are made
  • Added About window with version info and GitHub link

item.title: Version 0.2.0
item.description:
• Added auto-update via Sparkle — future updates install with one click
  • Added "Check for Updates" menu item
